title: Solid, liquid, gas sorting table
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: States of matter (Marvellous Medicine and How Far Can Sound Travel?)
source: Seeded from science/y4 lesson 1 (Solid, liquid, gas sorting table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 1: Solids, liquids and gases. To understand how solids, liquids and gases are different

blocks.title: Sort into: Solid / Liquid / Gas
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Solid, Liquid, Gas.
blocks.answer: Solid: brick; sand; ice. Liquid: milk; honey; oil. Gas: steam; air in a balloon

questions.q: Is honey a solid or a liquid?
questions.a: A liquid: it flows (slowly) and takes the shape of its container.
questions.model: Ask: does it keep its shape? No. Does it flow? Yes, slowly. Things that flow are liquids. So honey is a liquid.

questions.q: Why is sand a solid even though it pours?
questions.a: Each grain is a tiny solid that keeps its own shape.

questions.q: Which state can be squashed easily?
Core: Make a three-column table (solid, liquid, gas). Add four things from your home to each column.
questions.a: For example: solid: spoon, table, rice, soap; liquid: water, oil, juice, vinegar; gas: air, steam, the air in a ball, cooking smells.
questions.model: Teacher does one of each first: spoon (solid, keeps its shape), oil (liquid, pours), air in a balloon (gas, fills the space).

questions.q: Extend: Write one sentence for each state starting 'A ... is ... because ...'
questions.a: For example: A spoon is a solid because it keeps its shape.

questions.q: Stretch: Is toothpaste a solid or a liquid? Give your reasons.
questions.a: Accept a reasoned answer: it flows when squeezed (like a liquid) but holds its shape on the brush (like a solid).

questions.q: Which state spreads out to fill any space?
Big question: how can we tell if something is a solid, a liquid or a gas?
questions.a: Solids keep their shape; liquids flow and take the container's shape; gases spread out to fill any space.
